validity.recommendation: Keep the row; it is a real gas line. Rename toward 'North Rumaila NGL Plant - Khor Al-Zubair (KAZ) broadcut/gas export pipeline' and fix owner/specs per the attribution and spec findings below.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE = CONFIRMED as a real gas pipeline, independent of GEM. The sheet's ONLY citation is OPEC Annual Statistics Bulletin 2012 p.75 (a generic aggregate table that does not name this pipeline, and predates the current infrastructure) - that alone is an existence flag, but multiple independent operator/industry sources DO confirm a gas line in exactly this corridor. Basrah Gas Company (BGC) operates ~550 km of gas/liquids pipelines running from Khor al-Zubair to Rumaila with 23 compressor stations (basrahgas.com). The Basrah NGL expansion scope is described as 'an 80 km broadcut export to the BGC KAZ facility' from BGC's North Rumaila NGL plant, plus a 13.7 km feed-gas line and a 10.2 km dry-gas line to the Iraqi grid (china.aiddata.org, dmsuniverse). Oil & Gas Journal independently documents the North Rumaila (NR) NGL plant and the ~1,800 km BGC gathering/processing network feeding the KAZ NGL plant. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas line (rich gas / 'broadcut' NGL-feedstock export between the North Rumaila and KAZ NGL plants), NOT one of the crude/NGL oil lines in the GulfPub Iraq oil roster - so no oil/gas misclassification. Caveat: it functions as an inter-plant broadcut/NGL-feed export line rather than a dry sales-gas transmission trunk, but tracking it as a gas pipeline is defensible. DUPLICATE: checked against the 36-row Iraq gas roster - the other Khor al-Zubair lines are physically distinct (P1850 Khor Al-Zubair-Hartha 24-in/77 km; P6824 Shouibah-KAZ 10/8-in; P7435 KAZ-Shatt Al Arab 42-in/40 km). None share North Rumaila as an endpoint, so P2234 is not a relabel/segment double-count.

validity.recommendation: Change operator/owner from 'Iraq Ministry of Oil 100%' to Basrah Gas Company (operator); ownership is a JV - Govt of Iraq / South Gas Company 51%, Shell 44%, Mitsubishi 5%. Confirm the exact owning entity before applying.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists Owner1 = 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' at 100%. The North Rumaila and KAZ NGL plants and the interconnecting gas/broadcut pipelines are operated by Basrah Gas Company, a 25-year JV: Government of Iraq / South Gas Company 51%, Royal Dutch Shell 44%, Mitsubishi 5% (basrahgas.com, china.aiddata.org, enerdata). 'Iraq Ministry of Oil 100%' is at best imprecise (the state stake is held via South Gas Company and is 51%, not 100%) and omits the 49% Shell+Mitsubishi ownership. This is an attribution error/oversimplification.

validity.recommendation: Do NOT keep Diameter=42 in and Capacity=10 bcm/y as green. Diameter is unverified and appears conflated with North Rumaila CRUDE export figures; capacity has no matching independent source. Length 87 km vs independent ~80 km is a minor delta.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC audit vs independent sources: (1) LENGTH - GEM=87 km; the independent BGC/NGL-project descriptions give the North Rumaila->KAZ broadcut export line as '80 km' (china.aiddata.org, dmsuniverse). 80 vs 87 km is a small, tolerable delta - keep as caveat. (2) DIAMETER - GEM=42 in has NO independent gas source. The only 42-inch figures I found in this area are CRUDE OIL infrastructure: the North Rumaila crude pump station discharges at 42 in into a 48-in export line to Al Faw (enka.com), and Khor Al Amaya's crude export line is 42 in. The West Qurna->NR feed-gas line is documented at 40-in OD (Oil & Gas Journal). So the 42-in value looks conflated with crude oil pipe and is unverified for this gas line - flag it. (3) CAPACITY - GEM=10 bcm/y (~970 MMscfd). No independent source gives a single-line 10 bcm/y figure; the entire BGC multi-field system is rated 1.4 bcf/d (~14.5 bcm/y) across Rumaila+West Qurna 1+Zubair (china.aiddata.org). 10 bcm/y for one export line is plausible but unconfirmed - do not treat as corroborated.

Fuel source is Rumaila (North Rumaila) field associated gas, gathered via the North Rumaila NGL plant. Confirmed independently.

Endpoints confirmed as North Rumaila NGL plant -> KAZ (Khor Al-Zubair) NGL facility, both in Basrah governorate. This refines the sheet's generic StartLocation 'Rumela Oil field' / EndLocation 'Khor Al Zubair'. The 80 km broadcut export runs from BGC's North Rumaila NGL plant to the KAZ facility.

routes.corridor_desc: The line runs southeast/east across western and southern Basrah governorate from the North Rumaila NGL plant in the Rumaila field (near the Iraq-Kuwait border area) to the Khor al-Zubair industrial port/NGL complex south of Basra city. Independent descriptions put the North Rumaila->KAZ broadcut export leg at ~80 km (GEM says 87 km). Endpoints are well-established named facilities; the intermediate alignment is inferred (likely following the existing BGC pipeline corridor and roads west/south of Basra and Az Zubair), not surveyed. Straight-line distance between the two endpoints is ~65-70 km, consistent with an 80-87 km routed length.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named facilities: North Rumaila NGL plant (in the well-documented Rumaila field, whose center is ~30.4N 47.35E; the northern/NGL-plant area ~30.5N) and the Khor al-Zubair NGL complex/port (KAZ NGL plant documented as ~30 km south of Basra; Khor al-Zubair town at ~30.19N 47.88E). Coordinates are APPROXIMATE facility locations derived from those named places, marked as such - not surveyed and not fabricated. Az Zubair town (~30.39N 47.71E) is offered as a corridor-bounding waypoint, not a confirmed on-route point. No public GeoJSON of the exact alignment was found; propose 'medium' accuracy because endpoints are solid but the trace is inferred. Do NOT auto-apply - route to a human routes-repo branch.

summary: P2234 is a REAL BGC gas line (North Rumaila NGL plant -> Khor al-Zubair NGL facility, ~80 km broadcut export), correctly classified as gas and not a duplicate; but owner is wrong (BGC JV: SGC 51%/Shell 44%/Mitsubishi 5%, not Iraq MoO 100%) and specs are shaky (42-in diameter looks conflated with crude infrastructure and is unverified; 10 bcm/y capacity unconfirmed).
